title: Four Hundred Years in the Water: The Slow Life of a Plastic Bottle
title_zh: 在水里待四百年：一只塑料瓶的漫长一生
intro_zh: 本文约 516 词，围绕塑料污染与海洋保护展开，含 6 个 CET-4 核心词（volunteers, currents, debris, swallow, absorb, release），句子难度中等，适合四级阅读训练。

paragraphs.en: On a windy Saturday in April, sixty volunteers spread out along a two-kilometre stretch of beach near Xiamen, a city on China's southeast coast. In three hours they filled 214 bags. Most of what they picked up was not the romantic rubbish of old stories — glass bottles and paper — but light, bright plastic: bottle caps, straws, shopping bags and fragments too small to name.
paragraphs.zh: 四月一个多风的星期六，六十名志愿者在厦门（中国东南沿海的一座城市）附近一段两公里长的海滩上分散开来。三个小时里，他们装满了 214 个袋子。他们捡到的东西大多不是老故事里那种“浪漫的垃圾”——玻璃瓶和纸——而是轻飘飘、颜色鲜艳的塑料：瓶盖、吸管、购物袋，以及小到无法命名的碎片。

paragraphs.en: Those bags are a tiny sample of a much larger flow. Researchers estimate that about 11 million tonnes of plastic waste reach the ocean every year. That is roughly one rubbish truck emptied into the sea every minute. If nothing changes, some scientists expect the total to triple by 2040, because plastic production keeps rising while recycling rates stay low.
paragraphs.zh: 这些袋子只是一股更大洪流中的极小样本。研究人员估计，每年约有 1100 万吨塑料垃圾进入海洋，大致相当于每分钟有一辆垃圾车把垃圾倒进海里。如果情况不变，一些科学家预计到 2040 年这一总量将增至三倍，因为塑料产量持续上升，而回收率始终偏低。

paragraphs.en: Where does it come from? Studies suggest that a small number of rivers carry a large share — perhaps a quarter of the total comes from just a few major river systems in Asia. Packaging is the biggest single category, followed by fishing gear: nets, ropes and floats that are lost or thrown away at sea.
paragraphs.zh: 这些塑料从哪来？研究显示，少数几条河流输送了其中很大一部分——也许总量的四分之一只来自亚洲的几大水系。包装是最大的单一类别，其次是渔具：在海上丢失或被丢弃的渔网、绳索和浮标。

paragraphs.en: Once in the water, plastic does not stay where it falls. Ocean currents act like slow conveyor belts, carrying floating waste thousands of kilometres. In the North Pacific, rotating currents gather bottles and nets into a loose, cloudy field often called the Great Pacific Garbage Patch, an area some estimates put at 1.6 million square kilometres.
paragraphs.zh: 一旦进入水中，塑料并不会停在它落下的地方。洋流就像缓慢的传送带，把漂浮的垃圾带到数千公里之外。在北太平洋，旋转的洋流把瓶子和渔网聚集成一片松散、浑浊的区域，常被称为“太平洋垃圾带”，有估算认为其面积达 160 万平方公里。

paragraphs.en: Sunlight and waves then break the material into debris too small to see. These fragments, less than five millimetres across, are called microplastics. They have now been found in sea ice, in deep-sea sediment, in Arctic snow — and in the stomachs of animals sold in markets. A single thin plastic bag can shed millions of them in a few weeks.
paragraphs.zh: 随后阳光和海浪把这种材料分解成小到看不见的碎片。这些直径不足五毫米的碎片被称为微塑料。如今人们已在海冰、深海沉积物、北极的雪中找到它们——也在市场上出售的动物胃里找到。一只薄塑料袋在几周内就能释放出数百万个这样的颗粒。

paragraphs.en: The damage is easy to picture. Sea turtles swallow floating bags because they look like jellyfish. Seabirds feed small pieces to their chicks; one study of dead birds found that nine out of ten had plastic in their stomachs. Whales filter thousands of litres of water a day and take in plastic along with the food. Scientists estimate that more than 700 species have been affected.
paragraphs.zh: 造成的伤害很容易想象。海龟会吞下漂浮的袋子，因为它们看起来像水母。海鸟把小碎片喂给雏鸟；一项对死亡海鸟的研究发现，十只中有九只胃里有塑料。鲸每天过滤数千升海水，在获取食物的同时也把塑料吃进肚里。科学家估计已有 700 多个物种受到影响。

paragraphs.en: There is a chemical problem too. Plastics absorb pollutants such as PCB from the surrounding water, so a floating fragment can carry a concentrated dose of poison. When fish eat it, those chemicals may release into their bodies and move up the food chain toward us.
paragraphs.zh: 还有化学层面的问题。塑料会从周围水中吸附 PCB 等污染物，因此一片漂浮的碎片可能携带高度浓缩的毒素。当鱼吃下它时，这些化学物质可能释放到鱼体内，并沿着食物链层层上移，最终朝我们而来。

paragraphs.en: The good news is that this is one pollution problem we can actually see, measure and reduce. Deposit-return schemes in Norway and Germany take back more than 90% of bottles. Barriers stop waste in rivers before it reaches the sea; in Kenya, a simple river skimmer collected hundreds of tonnes in its first year. Beach clean-ups, run by volunteers, remove what is already there and provide data that scientists use.
paragraphs.zh: 好消息是，这是一个我们确实看得见、测得出、也减得少的污染问题。挪威和德国的押金回收制度回收了超过 90% 的瓶子。拦污设施在垃圾进入海洋之前就把它们挡在河里；在肯尼亚，一台简易的河道清捞设备第一年就收集了数百吨垃圾。由志愿者开展的海滩清理，既清走了已经存在的垃圾，也提供了科学家可用的数据。

paragraphs.en: No single action fixes the ocean. But a bottle that is refilled, returned or recycled never begins its four-hundred-year journey. The sea is patient; it is also slow to repair. Every choice made on land decides what the water will hold for the next generation.
paragraphs.zh: 没有哪一项单独的行动能治好海洋。但一只被重新灌装、被回收退还或被循环利用的瓶子，就永远不会开始它长达四百年的旅程。海洋很有耐心，但它修复得也很慢。陆地上的每一个选择，都在决定下一代的海水里将留下什么。

questions.q: According to the passage, what is the biggest single category of plastic waste entering the ocean?
questions.explain: 细节题。第三段明确说“Packaging is the biggest single category, followed by fishing gear”，即包装是最大的单一类别，渔具次之。玻璃瓶和纸是志愿者在海滩上捡到的“老式垃圾”，不是入海塑料的最大来源。

questions.q: Why do sea turtles swallow floating plastic bags?
options: Because the bags smell like their usual food.
Because the bags are small enough to be eaten safely.
Because the bags look similar to jellyfish, one of their foods.
Because they are forced to eat plastic when real food is gone.
questions.explain: 细节题。第六段说海龟吞下漂浮的袋子“because they look like jellyfish”，即塑料袋外形像水母，被海龟误认作食物。其余选项文中没有依据。

questions.q: The word 'shed' in paragraph 5 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: 词义题。第五段说一只薄塑料袋在几周内可以 “shed millions of them（微塑料）”，语境指塑料袋不断脱落、产生出大量微小颗粒，因此与 produce and drop 最接近。absorb 和 store 与“碎片被释放出来”的意思相反。

questions.q: What does the author mainly want to tell readers in the last paragraph?
options: The ocean will repair itself quickly if we simply wait.
Only governments and big companies can solve this problem.
Beach clean-ups are the most effective solution of all.
Ordinary choices about bottles and recycling still matter.
questions.explain: 主旨/推断题。最后一段强调没有单一行动能解决海洋问题，但一只被重复使用或回收的瓶子就不会开始它四百年的旅程，说明普通人的日常选择依然重要。文中明确说海洋“修复得也很慢”，与 A 相反；B、C 均属过度或片面推断。
